artists.biography: The Wannadies were an alternative rock band formed in 1988 in Skellefteå, Sweden.  The bands initial line-up featured Pär Wiksten (vocals, guitars), Christina Bergmark (keyboards, vocals), Stefan Schönfeldt (guitars) and his younger brother Frederick Schönfeldt (bass) with Gunnar Karlsson (drums) and Björn Malmquist (violin). Karlsson was later replaced by Erik Dahlgren.  Early influences included Australian band The Go-Betweens as well as The Sisters of Mercy.  The band released six studio albums in their 21 year career including the commercially successful Be A Girl (1994) and Bagsy Me (1997).  Part-way through recording their seventh studio album the band officially announced their split in April 2009 with Pär Wiksten going solo.

perplexity.description:
Bagsy Me is the fourth studio album by Swedish rock band The Wannadies, originally released in 1997. The album showcases the band's signature blend of melodic alternative rock and pop, characterized by catchy hooks, jangly guitar lines, and harmonious vocals. Produced by Nille Perned, Per Sunding, and Kjell Nästén, Bagsy Me features a polished yet energetic sound that highlights the group's knack for crafting accessible, radio-friendly tracks without sacrificing their indie sensibility.

Within The Wannadies' discography, Bagsy Me stands as a pivotal release, marking their breakthrough in the UK and broader European markets. It includes some of their most well-known songs, such as "You and Me Song," which gained international recognition. The album was released on Indolent Records and later reissued by Music On Vinyl, but its original 1997 release established the band's reputation for combining pop sensibilities with rock energy. While Bagsy Me did not achieve major chart success, it received positive critical attention for its consistency and melodic strength, solidifying its status as a fan favorite and a key album in the band's career.
